display.title: Parshas Zachor: Why We Remember Amalek
display.summary_short: Why everyone must hear Parshas Zachor before Purim, how Haman came from Amalek, and how the Torah learning of 22,000 children brought his downfall.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show for the Shabbos before Purim. Uncle Yossi explains that besides the weekly sedra, the Torah reading includes Parshas Zachor, three verses from Devarim chapter 25, and that everyone, boys and girls, men and women, must be in shul to hear them. All the nations trembled after the miracles of the Exodus, yet the small nation of Amalek dared to attack the Jewish people and was defeated. We remember Amalek because in every generation someone tries to do what Amalek wanted, and Hashem saves us. That is why we read it right before Purim: Haman was a descendant of Amalek. When Mordechai heard of Haman's plot, he gathered 22,000 children and taught them Torah, and their pure voices brought Haman's downfall. Today, too, children who learn Torah, make brachos, give tzedakah and pray can bring Moshiach.
display.lesson: Remember Amalek and trust that Hashem saves us in every generation; children's Torah and mitzvos have the power to bring Moshiach.
